cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: T returns text arguments unchanged
cases.expected_note: Verbatim from Microsoft: 'If value is or refers to text, T returns value.' The page's own example returns Rainfall for a cell holding that text

cases.description: DIVERGENCE PROBE: a number is not text, so T returns empty text rather than the number
cases.expected_note: Verbatim from Microsoft: 'If value does not refer to text, T returns "" (empty text)', and the page's example for the value 19 says 'Because the second value is a number, empty text is returned'. An engine that coerced the number to a string would return "19" instead

cases.description: A logical value is also not text, so the result is empty text
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's example table covers this case explicitly: 'Because the third value is a logical value, empty text is returned'. There is no TRUE -> "TRUE" coercion

cases.description: A reference to a cell holding text returns that text
cases.expected_note: The referenced value is text, so T passes it through unchanged

cases.description: A reference to a cell holding a number returns empty text
cases.expected_note: The referenced value is a number, which is not text, so T returns ""

cases.description: An error value passed to T propagates rather than becoming empty text
cases.expected_note: Error values propagate through T; the argument itself evaluates to #DIV/0! and that error is the result of the whole expression
